At 0249A the GALLICA copy prints 'ut videntes non videant, et audientes nos intelligant (Isa. VI)'; the ARCHIVE copy, read as an IMAGE and not merely as OCR, prints 'ut videntes non vident, et audientes non intelligant'. Our TEI agrees with Gallica at both words. Per the standing rule that where two clean copies differ there is no one to accuse, NO PATCH and NO [sic:]; the English renders the Gallica reading our TEI carries, and a [var:] records the received text. This is the PL 114 'two printings, not two photographs' shape appearing in PL 113. Also confirmed as printed: 'vel a bucca' at 0249A closing with NO terminal stop; '(GREG. lib.
